claim: Isthmin-1 (Ism1) mitigates diabetes by increasing adipocyte and skeletal muscle glucose uptake by activating the PI3K-Akt pathway.
source: The secreted protein isthmin-1 (Ism1) mitigates diabetes by increasing adipocyte and skeletal muscle glucose uptake by activating the PI3K-Akt pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Jiang et al., 2021) and represents established findings from prior research.

claim: Ism1 and insulin converge on common targets but have distinct cellular actions suggesting divergence in downstream intracellular signaling pathways.
source: However, while both Ism1 and insulin converge on these common targets, Ism1 has distinct cellular actions suggesting divergence in downstream intracellular signaling pathways.
evidence: This is based on inference from observed differences in cellular actions between Ism1 and insulin.

claim: There is a 53% overlap between Ism1 and insulin signaling.
source: We identify a 53% overlap between Ism1 and insulin signaling and Ism1-mediated phosphoproteome-wide alterations in ~450 proteins that are not shared with insulin.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomic data analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ism1 induces phosphoproteome-wide alterations in approximately 450 proteins that are not shared with insulin.
source: We identify a 53% overlap between Ism1 and insulin signaling and Ism1-mediated phosphoproteome-wide alterations in ~450 proteins that are not shared with insulin.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomic data analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ism1 signaling network includes several unknown phosphorylation sites on proteins related to protein translation, mTOR pathway, and muscle function.
source: Interestingly, we find several unknown phosphorylation sites on proteins related to protein translation, mTOR pathway, and, unexpectedly, muscle function in the Ism1 signaling network.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomic data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ism1 ablation in mice results in lower muscle protein levels under fed and fasted conditions.
source: Physiologically, Ism1 ablation in mice results in altered proteostasis, including lower muscle protein levels under fed and fasted conditions, reduced amino acid incorporation into proteins, and reduced phosphorylation of the key protein synthesis effectors Akt and downstream mTORC1 targets.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from Ism1-KO mice shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Ism1 ablation in mice results in reduced amino acid incorporation into proteins.
source: Physiologically, Ism1 ablation in mice results in altered proteostasis, including lower muscle protein levels under fed and fasted conditions, reduced amino acid incorporation into proteins, and reduced phosphorylation of the key protein synthesis effectors Akt and downstream mTORC1 targets.
evidence: This is supported by [35S]-methionine incorporation data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Ism1 ablation in mice results in reduced phosphorylation of the key protein synthesis effectors Akt and downstream mTORC1 targets.
source: Physiologically, Ism1 ablation in mice results in altered proteostasis, including lower muscle protein levels under fed and fasted conditions, reduced amino acid incorporation into proteins, and reduced phosphorylation of the key protein synthesis effectors Akt and downstream mTORC1 targets.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Metabolic disorders such as diabetes are associated with accelerated loss of skeletal muscle protein content.
source: As metabolic disorders such as diabetes are associated with accelerated loss of skeletal muscle protein content, these studies define a non-canonical mechanism by which this antidiabetic circulating protein controls muscle biology.
evidence: This is based on established scientific knowledge about diabetes and muscle protein loss.

claim: Hormonal signaling through protein phosphorylation is one of the most important post-translational modifications allowing for rapid changes in cellular metabolic states.
source: Hormonal signaling through protein phosphorylation is one of the most important post-translational modifications allowing for rapid changes in cellular metabolic states (Humphrey et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Humphrey et al., 2015.

claim: Metabolic stressors such as diabetes or fasting can lead to pronounced physiological and cellular adaptations in protein regulation.
source: Metabolic stressors such as diabetes or fasting can lead to pronounced physiological and cellular adaptations in protein regulation (Powers et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Powers et al., 2009.

claim: Pathological conditions can result in muscle atrophy, a net loss of muscle mass, which is highly associated with morbidity.
source: Consequently, pathological conditions can result in muscle atrophy, a net loss of muscle mass, which is highly associated with morbidity (Cohen et al., 2015; Jackman and Kandarian, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cohen et al., 2015 and Jackman and Kandarian, 2004.

claim: Muscle strength is reduced in individuals with insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes.
source: Muscle strength is reduced in individuals with insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes (Andersen et al., 2004; Park et al., 2007), and muscle weakness is even a diagnostic predictor of diabetes (Peterson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Andersen et al., 2004 and Park et al., 2007.

claim: Muscle weakness is a diagnostic predictor of diabetes.
source: Muscle strength is reduced in individuals with insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes (Andersen et al., 2004; Park et al., 2007), and muscle weakness is even a diagnostic predictor of diabetes (Peterson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Peterson et al., 2016.

claim: Skeletal muscle represents up to half of the total mass in normal-weight individuals.
source: Skeletal muscle is the most abundant tissue in humans, representing up to half of the total mass in normal-weight individuals (Janssen et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Janssen et al., 2000.

claim: Skeletal muscle controls whole-body energy expenditure and nutrient homeostasis.
source: As a major organ for glycogen storage and insulin-mediated glucose uptake, skeletal muscle controls whole-body energy expenditure and nutrient homeostasis (Deshmukh, 2016; Shulman et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Deshmukh, 2016 and Shulman et al., 1990.

claim: Growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) stimulate muscle fiber size (hypertrophy).
source: Importantly, skeletal muscle also acts as a protein reservoir that is highly responsive to anabolic or catabolic hormonal stimulation, including growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1), both of which stimulate muscle fiber size (hypertrophy) (Moro et al., 2016; Velloso, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Moro et al., 2016 and Velloso, 2008.

claim: The Akt/mTORC1 signaling pathway promotes protein synthesis and robustly induces muscle hypertrophy upon stimulation by growth factors or amino acids.
source: The most well-described anabolic signaling pathway that promotes protein synthesis requires Akt/mTORC1 signaling, which robustly induces muscle hypertrophy upon stimulation by growth factors or amino acids (Bodine et al., 2001; Glass, 2011; Lai et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bodine et al., 2001, Glass, 2011, and Lai et al., 2004.

claim: In both flies and mammals, the PI3K-Akt pathway controls cell size by increasing protein synthesis at the level of translation initiation.
source: In both flies (Scanga et al., 2000) and mammals (Edinger and Thompson, 2002), the PI3K-Akt pathway controls cell size by increasing protein synthesis at the level of translation initiation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Scanga et al., 2000 and Edinger and Thompson, 2002.

claim: Akt inhibits the catabolic function of FoxO family members, which upon phosphorylation are no longer able to enter the nucleus and turn on the transcription of atrophy genes.
source: Akt also inhibits the catabolic function of FoxO family members, which upon phosphorylation are no longer able to enter the nucleus and turn on the transcription of atrophy genes, including the E3 ubiquitin ligases MuRF1 and atrogin-1 (Bodine et al., 2001; Bodine and Baehr, 2014; Gomes et al., 2001; Lecker et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bodine et al., 2001, Bodine and Baehr, 2014, Gomes et al., 2001, and Lecker et al., 1999.

claim: Ism1 improves glucose tolerance and insulin resistance by phosphorylating AktS473, which mediates increased adipose and skeletal muscle glucose uptake.
source: We recently reported that the adipocyte-secreted protein isthmin-1 (Ism1) improves glucose tolerance and insulin resistance by phosphorylating AktS473, which mediates increased adipose and skeletal muscle glucose uptake (Jiang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: Ism1 adipose expression and circulating levels are elevated in mice and humans with obesity.
source: Ism1 adipose expression and circulating levels are elevated in mice and humans with obesity (Jiang et al., 2021; Ruiz-Ojeda et al., 2022), suggesting that the expression is under nutrient-sensing regulatory control.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jiang et al., 2021 and Ruiz-Ojeda et al., 2022.

claim: Ism1 administration to mice simultaneously prevents hepatic lipid accumulation while increasing protein synthesis in hepatocytes.
source: Intriguingly, Ism1 administration to mice simultaneously prevents hepatic lipid accumulation while increasing protein synthesis in hepatocytes (Jiang et al., 2021), demonstrating that Ism1 governs an anabolic pathway that is molecularly and functionally distinct from insulin.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: Ism1 induces specific Ism1-regulated phosphoproteome changes enriched for proteins controlling protein translation, mTOR signaling, and muscle function.
source: In this study, we find that Ism1 induces specific Ism1-regulated phosphoproteome changes enriched for proteins controlling protein translation, mTOR signaling, and muscle function.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomic data presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Ism1 is important to maintain skeletal muscle fiber size under fasting.
source: Furthermore, we show that Ism1 is important to maintain skeletal muscle fiber size under fasting, thereby defining a non-canonical mechanism by which Ism1 controls muscle biology.
evidence: This is supported by data from Ism1-KO mice shown in Figure 4.

claim: The PI3K-Akt pathway is a key pathway of convergence for ligands that activate receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), including insulin.
source: The PI3K-Akt pathway is a key pathway of convergence for ligands that activate receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), including insulin (Humphrey et al., 2013; Luo et al., 2003; Zhao et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Humphrey et al., 2013, Luo et al., 2003, and Zhao et al., 2020.

claim: Ism1 increases glucose uptake into fat and muscle by potently activating PI3K-Akt signaling across a range of mouse and human cell types.
source: We recently identified Ism1 as an adipose-secreted protein that increases glucose uptake into fat and muscle by potently activating PI3K-Akt signaling across a range of mouse and human cell types, but unlike insulin, does not induce de novo lipogenesis (Jiang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: Unlike insulin, Ism1 does not induce de novo lipogenesis.
source: We recently identified Ism1 as an adipose-secreted protein that increases glucose uptake into fat and muscle by potently activating PI3K-Akt signaling across a range of mouse and human cell types, but unlike insulin, does not induce de novo lipogenesis (Jiang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: Approximately 7700 raw MS precursor ions (peptides) were acquired in the phosphoproteomic analysis.
source: In total, ~7700 raw MS precursor ions (peptides) were acquired, resulting in the identification of unique phosphopeptides on >5000 proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by the phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The phosphoproteomic analysis resulted in the identification of unique phosphopeptides on more than 5000 proteins.
source: In total, ~7700 raw MS precursor ions (peptides) were acquired, resulting in the identification of unique phosphopeptides on >5000 proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by the phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Principal component analysis (PCA) demonstrates high reproducibility between biological replicates and distinct separation of the Ism1- and insulin-treated groups compared with each other and the albumin control.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) demonstrates high reproducibility between biological replicates and distinct separation of the Ism1- and insulin-treated groups compared with each other and the albumin control (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the PCA plot shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Insulin induces phosphorylation of 654 phosphosites, out of which 347 phosphosites are also phosphorylated or dephosphorylated by Ism1.
source: Insulin induces phosphorylation of 654 phosphosites, out of which 347 phosphosites are also phosphorylated or dephosphorylated by Ism1 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the Venn diagram shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ism1 causes changes in the phosphorylation status of 445 proteins compared with BSA that are not shared with insulin and not previously described.
source: Remarkably, Ism1 causes changes in the phosphorylation status of 445 proteins compared with BSA that are not shared with insulin and not previously described (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the Venn diagram shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ism1 exclusively alters the phosphorylation status of proteins involved in the mTOR complex and muscle.
source: Interestingly, we find that Ism1 exclusively alters the phosphorylation status of proteins involved in the mTOR complex and muscle (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by the distribution diagram shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Ism1 does not induce the exact same targets in the insulin pathway as insulin.
source: This phosphoproteomic mapping shows that Ism1 does not induce the exact same targets in the insulin pathway as insulin (Figure 2A), which is entirely consistent with our previous study using phospho-tyrosine antibodies for the IR (Jiang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by the Venn diagram in Figure 2A and citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: Only insulin phosphorylates the InsR at Y1175/Y1163 while no significant phosphorylation is induced by Ism1.
source: For example, only insulin phosphorylates the InsR at Y1175/Y1163 while no significant phosphorylation is induced by Ism1 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the abundance data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Ism1 induces phosphorylation of some of the same proteins as insulin, including IR substrates Irs1 and Irs2, but with distinct phosphosite patterns.
source: Interestingly, Ism1 induces phosphorylation of some of the same proteins as insulin, including IR substrates Irs1 and Irs2, but with distinct phosphosite patterns.
evidence: This is supported by the phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Irs2 was phosphorylated at T347 by insulin but at S588 by Ism1.
source: For example, Irs2 was phosphorylated at T347 by insulin but at S588 by Ism1 (Figure 1F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Insulin induces phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6 (Rps6), a regulator of protein synthesis downstream of mTOR.
source: Insulin induces phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6 (Rps6), a regulator of protein synthesis downstream of mTOR (Figure 2E and F), while Ism1 inhibits Rps6S236 and Rps6S240 phosphorylation (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: Ism1 inhibits Rps6S236 and Rps6S240 phosphorylation.
source: Insulin induces phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6 (Rps6), a regulator of protein synthesis downstream of mTOR (Figure 2E and F), while Ism1 inhibits Rps6S236 and Rps6S240 phosphorylation (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Ism1 induced phosphorylation of adenomatous polyposis coli (Apc)S1040.
source: Furthermore, Ism1 induced phosphorylation of several proteins shown to regulate muscle growth and fiber size, such as adenomatous polyposis coli (Apc)S1040(Chen et al., 2020; Parisi et al., 2015; Figure 2G), supervillin (Svil)S220 (Hedberg-Oldfors et al., 2020; Figure 2H), and FGF-receptor substrate 2 (Frs2)S327 (Chen and Friesel, 2009; Figure 2I).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2G and citations to Chen et al., 2020 and Parisi et al., 2015.

claim: Ism1 induced phosphorylation of supervillin (Svil)S220.
source: Furthermore, Ism1 induced phosphorylation of several proteins shown to regulate muscle growth and fiber size, such as adenomatous polyposis coli (Apc)S1040(Chen et al., 2020; Parisi et al., 2015; Figure 2G), supervillin (Svil)S220 (Hedberg-Oldfors et al., 2020; Figure 2H), and FGF-receptor substrate 2 (Frs2)S327 (Chen and Friesel, 2009; Figure 2I).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2H and citation to Hedberg-Oldfors et al., 2020.

claim: Ism1 induced phosphorylation of FGF-receptor substrate 2 (Frs2)S327.
source: Furthermore, Ism1 induced phosphorylation of several proteins shown to regulate muscle growth and fiber size, such as adenomatous polyposis coli (Apc)S1040(Chen et al., 2020; Parisi et al., 2015; Figure 2G), supervillin (Svil)S220 (Hedberg-Oldfors et al., 2020; Figure 2H), and FGF-receptor substrate 2 (Frs2)S327 (Chen and Friesel, 2009; Figure 2I).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2I and citation to Chen and Friesel, 2009.

claim: Frs2 is a lipid-anchored adapter protein and downstream mediator of signaling of multiple RTKs supporting the existence of a distinct Ism1 receptor.
source: Frs2 is also a lipid-anchored adapter protein and downstream mediator of signaling of multiple RTKs supporting the existence of a distinct Ism1 receptor (Zhou et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2009 and inference from the data.

claim: Eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit A (Eif3) was phosphorylated by insulin but not Ism1.
source: Interestingly, eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit A (Eif3), a complex-subunit playing a major role in translation initiation (Ma et al., 2022), was phosphorylated by insulin but not Ism1 (Figure 2J), while 60S ribosomal protein L12 (Rpl13) at S77 (Figure 2K) and 40S ribosomal protein S13-1 (Rps13a) at S237 (Figure 2L) and Rps3a at S238 (Figure 2M) were entirely dephosphorylated by both Ism1 and insulin.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2J and citation to Ma et al., 2022.

claim: 60S ribosomal protein L12 (Rpl13) at S77 and 40S ribosomal protein S13-1 (Rps13a) at S237 and Rps3a at S238 were entirely dephosphorylated by both Ism1 and insulin.
source: Interestingly, eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 subunit A (Eif3), a complex-subunit playing a major role in translation initiation (Ma et al., 2022), was phosphorylated by insulin but not Ism1 (Figure 2J), while 60S ribosomal protein L12 (Rpl13) at S77 (Figure 2K) and 40S ribosomal protein S13-1 (Rps13a) at S237 (Figure 2L) and Rps3a at S238 (Figure 2M) were entirely dephosphorylated by both Ism1 and insulin.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2K, 2L, and 2M.

claim: Ribosomal protein S6 kinase alpha-5 (Rps6ka5) was phosphorylated by both Ism1 and insulin at S375.
source: Lastly, ribosomal protein S6 kinase alpha-5 (Rps6ka5), a known mTOR substrate (Chauvin et al., 2014). was phosphorylated by both Ism1 and insulin at S375 (Figure 2N).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2N and citation to Chauvin et al., 2014.

claim: GO enrichment analysis found associations with metabolic processes such as glucose and lipid metabolism.
source: We found associations previously linked to Ism1, including metabolic processes such as glucose and lipid metabolism (Jiang et al., 2021; Ruiz-Ojeda et al., 2022), nervous system development (Osório et al., 2014; Pera et al., 2002), and the immune system (Lam et al., 2022; Li et al., 2021; Valle-Rios et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2021; Figure 2P).
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2P and citations to Jiang et al., 2021 and Ruiz-Ojeda et al., 2022.

claim: GO enrichment analysis found associations with nervous system development.
source: We found associations previously linked to Ism1, including metabolic processes such as glucose and lipid metabolism (Jiang et al., 2021; Ruiz-Ojeda et al., 2022), nervous system development (Osório et al., 2014; Pera et al., 2002), and the immune system (Lam et al., 2022; Li et al., 2021; Valle-Rios et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2021; Figure 2P).
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2P and citations to Osório et al., 2014 and Pera et al., 2002.

claim: GO enrichment analysis found associations with the immune system.
source: We found associations previously linked to Ism1, including metabolic processes such as glucose and lipid metabolism (Jiang et al., 2021; Ruiz-Ojeda et al., 2022), nervous system development (Osório et al., 2014; Pera et al., 2002), and the immune system (Lam et al., 2022; Li et al., 2021; Valle-Rios et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2021; Figure 2P).
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2P and citations to Lam et al., 2022, Li et al., 2021, Valle-Rios et al., 2014, and Wu et al., 2021.

claim: Several pathways associated with muscle, skeletal muscle, and cardiac muscle were identified in the Ism1 treatment group.
source: Intriguingly, also here, we identify several pathways associated with muscle, skeletal muscle, and cardiac muscle in the Ism1 treatment group (Figure 2P).
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2P.

claim: The PI3K-Akt pathway is known to promote anabolic programs in muscle cells.
source: Given the Ism1-induced muscle-signaling signature in 3T3-F442A cells and that the PI3K-Akt pathway is known to promote anabolic programs in muscle cells (Edinger and Thompson, 2002), muscle cell differentiation (Wilson and Rotwein, 2007), and skeletal muscle hypertrophy (Bodine et al., 2001; Jaiswal et al., 2019), we next asked whether Ism1 induces anabolic cellular signaling pathways in muscle cells.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Edinger and Thompson, 2002.

claim: The PI3K-Akt pathway is known to promote muscle cell differentiation.
source: Given the Ism1-induced muscle-signaling signature in 3T3-F442A cells and that the PI3K-Akt pathway is known to promote anabolic programs in muscle cells (Edinger and Thompson, 2002), muscle cell differentiation (Wilson and Rotwein, 2007), and skeletal muscle hypertrophy (Bodine et al., 2001; Jaiswal et al., 2019), we next asked whether Ism1 induces anabolic cellular signaling pathways in muscle cells.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wilson and Rotwein, 2007.

claim: The PI3K-Akt pathway is known to promote skeletal muscle hypertrophy.
source: Given the Ism1-induced muscle-signaling signature in 3T3-F442A cells and that the PI3K-Akt pathway is known to promote anabolic programs in muscle cells (Edinger and Thompson, 2002), muscle cell differentiation (Wilson and Rotwein, 2007), and skeletal muscle hypertrophy (Bodine et al., 2001; Jaiswal et al., 2019), we next asked whether Ism1 induces anabolic cellular signaling pathways in muscle cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bodine et al., 2001 and Jaiswal et al., 2019.

claim: In differentiated C2C12 myotubes, Ism1 induces phosphorylation of AktS473 and ribosomal S6S235/S236 starting at 5 min and remaining up to 4 hr.
source: In differentiated C2C12 myotubes, Ism1 induces phosphorylation of AktS473 and ribosomal S6S235/S236 starting at 5 min and remaining up to 4 hr (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The effect of Ism1 on Akt signaling is robust but lower than that of the skeletal muscle hypertrophy hormone insulin-like growth factor-1 (Igf1).
source: The effect of Ism1 on Akt signaling is robust but lower than that of the skeletal muscle hypertrophy hormone insulin-like growth factor-1 (Igf1) (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Undifferentiated C2C12 myoblasts are responsive to Ism1 in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Similarly, undifferentiated C2C12 myoblasts are also responsive to Ism1 in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Ism1 treatment induced a 2.5-fold increase in protein synthesis as determined by [35S]-methionine incorporation into proteins.
source: Notably, Ism1 treatment induced a 2.5-fold increase in protein synthesis as determined by [35S]-methionine incorporation into proteins (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by [35S]-methionine incorporation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Igf1 treatment resulted in a threefold induction in protein synthesis.
source: As expected, Igf1 treatment resulted in a threefold induction in protein synthesis (Figure 3D), and the combined Igf1 and Ism1 treatment did not induce protein synthesis further, suggesting that the maximal capacity of protein synthesis has been reached under these conditions.
evidence: This is supported by [35S]-methionine incorporation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The combined Igf1 and Ism1 treatment did not induce protein synthesis further, suggesting that the maximal capacity of protein synthesis has been reached under these conditions.
source: As expected, Igf1 treatment resulted in a threefold induction in protein synthesis (Figure 3D), and the combined Igf1 and Ism1 treatment did not induce protein synthesis further, suggesting that the maximal capacity of protein synthesis has been reached under these conditions.
evidence: This is based on inference from the [35S]-methionine incorporation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: mTORC1/2 inhibition with rapamycin inhibits Ism1-induced signaling in 3T3-F442A cells, demonstrating that intact mTOR activity is required for the signaling capacity of Ism1.
source: Previous data showed that mTORC1/2 inhibition with rapamycin inhibits Ism1-induced signaling in 3T3-F442A cells, demonstrating that intact mTOR activity is required for the signaling capacity of Ism1 (Jiang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: Low-dose rapamycin inhibits Ism1-induced protein synthesis, establishing that the functional effects are directly linked to the signaling cascade induced by Ism1.
source: Importantly, low-dose rapamycin also inhibits Ism1-induced protein synthesis, establishing that the functional effects are directly linked to the signaling cascade induced by Ism1 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by [35S]-methionine incorporation data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Rapamycin has inhibitory effects on muscle hypertrophy during anabolic conditions.
source: These data align with the inhibitory effects of rapamycin on muscle hypertrophy during anabolic conditions (Pallafacchina et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pallafacchina et al., 2002.

claim: Ism1 induces a signaling cascade that requires intact mTOR signaling to induce protein synthesis in muscle cells.
source: In conclusion, Ism1 induces a signaling cascade that requires intact mTOR signaling to induce protein synthesis in muscle cells.
evidence: This is based on inference from the rapamycin inhibition data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Skeletal muscle atrophy occurs when the protein degradation rate exceeds protein synthesis.
source: Skeletal muscle atrophy, a reduction in muscle mass, occurs when the protein degradation rate exceeds protein synthesis (Cohen et al., 2015; Jaiswal et al., 2019; Sandri et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cohen et al., 2015, Jaiswal et al., 2019, and Sandri et al., 2004.

claim: Ism1 controls glucose uptake into adipose tissue and skeletal muscle in mice.
source: We previously showed that Ism1 controls glucose uptake into adipose tissue and skeletal muscle in mice (Jiang et al., 2021), but the role of Ism1 in skeletal muscle function beyond glucose regulation has not been studied.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: Ism1 is broadly expressed, including highly in adipose tissue and blood.
source: Ism1 is broadly expressed, including highly in adipose tissue and blood (Jiang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: Ism1 is not expressed in muscle precursors or mature muscle cells.
source: By analyzing single-cell RNA sequencing data from murine skeletal muscle (Baht et al., 2020), we find that Ism1 is not expressed in muscle precursors or mature muscle cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and citation to Baht et al., 2020.

claim: Whole-body ablation of Ism1 in mice completely ablates blood levels of Ism1.
source: Therefore, we next sought to determine whether whole-body ablation of Ism1 in mice, in which blood levels of Ism1 are completely ablated (Jiang et al., 2021), resulted in changes to skeletal muscle mass.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: All fasted mice had a reduction in body weight compared with fed mice.
source: As expected, at dissection, all fasted mice had a reduction in body weight compared with fed mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by body weight data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Blood glucose levels were 150 mg/dl in the fed state, and <80 mg/dl in the fasted state.
source: Blood glucose levels were 150 mg/dl in the fed state, and <80 mg/dl in the fasted state (Figure 4C), but no differences were seen between genotypes.
evidence: This is supported by blood glucose data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: No differences in blood glucose levels were seen between WT and Ism1-KO genotypes.
source: Blood glucose levels were 150 mg/dl in the fed state, and <80 mg/dl in the fasted state (Figure 4C), but no differences were seen between genotypes.
evidence: This is supported by blood glucose data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Muscle tissue morphology was similar between the WT and Ism1-KO genotypes.
source: Muscle tissue morphology was similar between the genotypes, but the muscle fiber size was notably smaller in the Ism1-KO quadriceps muscles (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The muscle fiber size was notably smaller in the Ism1-KO quadriceps muscles.
source: Muscle tissue morphology was similar between the genotypes, but the muscle fiber size was notably smaller in the Ism1-KO quadriceps muscles (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The Ism1-KO quadriceps muscles demonstrate a robust shift in distribution to smaller muscle fiber size areas under both fed and fasted conditions.
source: Remarkably, fiber size area quantifications showed that the Ism1-KO quadriceps muscles demonstrate a robust shift in distribution to smaller muscle fiber size areas under both fed and fasted conditions (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by fiber size distribution data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Loss of Ism1 significantly reduces the cross-sectional area by 40% in the fed state and >20% in the fasted state.
source: On average, loss of Ism1 significantly reduces the cross-sectional area by 40% in the fed state and >20% in the fasted state (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The Ism1-KO mice had impaired muscle force.
source: While the heart weights (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), muscle weights (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), femur length (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), or total body weights (Figure 4B) of Ism1-KO mice were not significantly different from WT, the Ism1-KO mice had impaired muscle force (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by grip strength data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The heart weights, muscle weights, femur length, or total body weights of Ism1-KO mice were not significantly different from WT.
source: While the heart weights (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), muscle weights (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), femur length (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), or total body weights (Figure 4B) of Ism1-KO mice were not significantly different from WT, the Ism1-KO mice had impaired muscle force (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ism1 ablation leads to smaller skeletal muscle fiber size and loss of muscle strength.
source: In conclusion, these results show that Ism1 ablation leads to smaller skeletal muscle fiber size and loss of muscle strength.
evidence: This is based on inference from the data shown in Figures 4D-G.

claim: Ambulatory activity, respiratory exchange ratio (RER), energy expenditure as measured by VO2 consumption, or food intake are indistinguishable between WT and Ism1-KO mice when measured over a 48 hr period.

claim: The expression of Ppargc1a (Pgc1α) is unchanged in quadriceps muscle tissues from the Ism1-KO mice.

claim: General muscle markers, including the myosin heavy chain proteins Myh1, Myh2, Myh4, and Myh7, were not altered under fed conditions.

claim: Only Myh4 was reduced in the Ism1-KO mice under fasted conditions, suggesting that muscle fiber type is largely unaffected by Ism1 ablation.

claim: Ism1 regulates muscle fiber size and muscle strength without affecting the expression of mitochondrial complexes or whole-body energy expenditure.

claim: Quadriceps muscles from Ism1-KO mice have a significant reduction in total protein content compared with WT mice.

claim: Loss of Ism1 results in a significant reduction in muscle protein synthesis in mice.
source: WT and Ism1-KO mice were i.p. administered with [35S]-methionine for 2 hr, followed by protein precipitation, which demonstrates that loss of Ism1 results in a significant reduction in muscle protein synthesis in mice (Figure 6C).

claim: Under either fed or fasted conditions, muscles isolated from Ism1-KO mice have significantly increased transcript levels of atrophy genes FoxO1.

claim: Under either fed or fasted conditions, muscles isolated from Ism1-KO mice have significantly increased transcript levels of the FoxO target genes Cdkn1b, Eif4ebp1, and Ctsl.
source: Furthermore, under either fed or fasted conditions, muscles isolated from Ism1-KO mice have significantly increased transcript levels of atrophy genes FoxO1 (Figure 6D), the FoxO target genes Cdkn1b, Eif4ebp1, and Ctsl (Figure 6E), and ubiquitin ligase Fbxo30 compared with WT mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), and increased protein levels of the FoxO target p27 (Cdkn1b) (Zhang et al., 2011; Figure 6F).

claim: Muscles isolated from Ism1-KO mice have increased protein levels of the FoxO target p27 (Cdkn1b).

claim: Ism1 controls protein synthesis, and its loss is associated with elevated protein degradation gene expression.

claim: Loss of muscle-specific Akt1 and Akt2 leads to muscle atrophy.
source: Given that Ism1 activates the Akt pathway in myocytes in vitro, and that loss of muscle-specific Akt1 and Akt2 leads to muscle atrophy (Jaiswal et al., 2019), we next hypothesized that the mechanism behind the smaller muscle fiber size in the Ism1-KO mice is due to reduced Akt pathway activity.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jaiswal et al., 2019.

claim: Phosphorylation of AktS473, mTOR2448, and ribosomal S6S235/S236 are markedly decreased in Ism1-KO muscle compared with WT mice under both fed and fast conditions.
source: Indeed, we found that phosphorylation of AktS473, mTOR2448, and ribosomal S6S235/S236 are markedly decreased in Ism1-KO muscle compared with WT mice under both fed and fast conditions, providing an explanation for the lower protein synthesis rate (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Ism1-KO mice are indistinguishable from WT mice in the phosphorylation of IRS1 at S307.

claim: Ism1 is an anabolic regulator of protein synthesis and muscle strength by maintaining high Akt activity and protein synthesis in skeletal muscle.

claim: Akt has an established role in enhancing muscle hypertrophy and function.

claim: Ism1 activates Akt in multiple cell types, including human skeletal muscle cells.

claim: Ism1 increases glucose transport into both adipose tissue and skeletal muscle.

claim: While Ism1 does not directly phosphorylate the IR/IGFRs, Ism1 does induce phosphorylation of the IR substrate proteins (Irs).
source: Interestingly, while Ism1 does not directly phosphorylate the IR/IGFRs, Ism1 does induce phosphorylation of the IR substrate proteins (Irs), a feature that is shared with other endocrine hormones.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomic data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Phosphospecific regulation by distinct hormones can result in a diverse range of functional outcomes.
